slot.brief: Hard conceptual MCQ on elastic behaviour: compare stress-strain curves / breaking stress vs elastic limit of two wires of different lengths and cross-sections, identifying which statements about Young's modulus, elongation and breaking load hold true.

stem: Two wires $P$ and $Q$ have lengths $L$ and $2L$ and cross-sectional areas $A$ and $3A$. Their Young's moduli are $2Y$ and $Y$, elastic-limit stresses are $2\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_0$, and breaking stresses are $3\sigma_0$ and $2\sigma_0$, respectively. Which statements are true? I. $Y_P=2Y_Q$. II. At the same load $F=\sigma_0 A$, $\Delta\ell_P=\dfrac{3}{4}\Delta\ell_Q$. III. The breaking load of $Q$ is twice that of $P$. IV. The maximum elastic extension of $P$ is twice that of $Q$.

working:
$\Delta\ell=\dfrac{FL}{AY}$ gives $\dfrac{\Delta\ell_P}{\Delta\ell_Q}=\dfrac{1/(2Y)}{2/(3Y)}=\dfrac{3}{4}$. 
$F_{b,P}=3\sigma_0 A$; $F_{b,Q}=2\sigma_0(3A)=6\sigma_0 A$. 
$\Delta\ell_{\mathrm{el},P}=\dfrac{2\sigma_0}{2Y}L=\dfrac{\sigma_0L}{Y}$; $\Delta\ell_{\mathrm{el},Q}=\dfrac{\sigma_0}{Y}(2L)=\dfrac{2\sigma_0L}{Y}$.

Independent check: I: The moduli are given as 2Y and Y, so true. II: Using [?] [?] the extension ratio is [?]; evaluating gives 3/4, true. III: Breaking loads are 3σ₀A for P and 6σ₀A for Q, so true. IV: Maximum elastic extensions are σ₀L/Y for P and 2σ₀L/Y for Q, so false.
solution:
I is true since $Y_P=2Y_Q$. Using $\Delta\ell=\dfrac{FL}{AY}$ at $F=\sigma_0A$, $\dfrac{\Delta\ell_P}{\Delta\ell_Q}=\dfrac{1/(2Y)}{2/(3Y)}=\dfrac34$, so II is true.\\
$F_{b,P}=3\sigma_0A$ and $F_{b,Q}=2\sigma_0(3A)=6\sigma_0A$, so III is true. The elastic extensions are $\Delta\ell_{e,P}=\dfrac{\sigma_0L}{Y}$ and $\Delta\ell_{e,Q}=\dfrac{2\sigma_0L}{Y}$; IV is false. Hence, (B).
